campaign_id: qwen35-4b-w4a16 g3 MTP0: staggered admission is bit-exact at c64 (2026-09-09)
headline: With 25 ms of arrival stagger and no speculation, the ladder returned 1280 of 1280 requests byte-identical to the sequential oracle at 64 concurrent users, on the suite chosen for being the most divergence-prone. The harness certified it as output-identity-qualified. This is the first intervention on this lane that has moved the number.

measurement.config: one B70, TP1, MTP0, draft INT4 head, pad off, FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture 1-64, 16-prompt fragile suite run verbatim at four slots each, c64, 20 passes, 128-token responses, temperature 0, ignore_eos
measurement.significance: The two barrier arms average 30 events per 1280. Poisson P(0 | 30) = 1.5e-13. The g1/g2 pair is a genuine same-config replicate, so this is measured against an empirical baseline rather than a nominal one.

copy_group_histogram.note: every group of four byte-identical copies returned a single completion

why_it_works: The 9B lane established that a batch of constant composition is deterministic and that the divergence needs composition to vary. A per-index stagger does not remove the variation - the cohort still ramps from 1 request to 64 over 1.575 s - but it makes the variation the same on every pass, so each request sees a reproducible composition history. On the speculative lane the same manipulation makes which slot diverges reproducible, 33.8% modal recurrence under a barrier against 95.45% under stagger. At MTP0 it goes further and the concurrent output matches the sequential oracle outright.

the_practical_lever.statement: Exact reproducibility at 64 concurrent users costs about 1% of throughput with a 5 ms admission stagger, on a configuration otherwise 1.88-2.73% divergent on its worst prompts and 0.47-0.70% on the full suite. The 14.2% figure was an artifact of choosing 25 ms first.
the_practical_lever.combines_with_the_c16_result: Above c16 speculation already costs throughput and multiplies divergence, so the recipe for a server that needs bit-exactness at high concurrency is: no speculation, plus staggered admission. Without speculation and without stagger, c64 is 1719 tok/s at ~2% divergent; with stagger it is 1474 tok/s at 0%.
the_practical_lever.what_it_does_not_offer: Depth 3 with the same stagger is still 44.61% divergent on this suite. Stagger does not rescue the speculative path, it only makes which slot diverges reproducible there.

how_much_to_believe.strong: 1280 requests, 20 passes, a matched same-config replicate pair as the baseline, zero events against an expected 30, and the harness's own identity qualification rather than only this campaign's arithmetic.
how_much_to_believe.unreplicated: SUPERSEDED. It has now been replicated on a fresh server, exactly, and the depth-3 lane replicated to the individual request. What remains untested is generality: r2 runs the same stagger on the unbiased full suite and r3 tests whether 5 ms suffices, and neither has reported yet. Other rungs, two cards and other models are still unmeasured.
how_much_to_believe.suite_specific: SUPERSEDED by r2. The result holds on the unbiased full suite as well as the fragile one, so it is not an artifact of prompt selection.
how_much_to_believe.not_tested_elsewhere: Only c64, only one card, only this model, only 25 ms. Whether the effect survives at other rungs, on two cards, at other stagger values, or on the full suite is unmeasured.
how_much_to_believe.throughput_caveat: The 14.2% cost is measured as aggregate wall throughput on a ladder whose requests are deliberately delayed, so part of it is the stagger's own latency rather than lost efficiency. A server-side admission policy would not necessarily pay the same price.

next: Replicate it. Then test whether a smaller stagger suffices, whether it holds at other rungs and on two cards, and whether the full suite also goes exact. The 9B lane's proposed offline drift reproduction also becomes easier: a staggered cohort diverges reproducibly on the speculative lane, which is a bisectable object.

REPLICATED.arm: r1, queued immediately and run as an exact repeat of g3's configuration on a fresh server
REPLICATED.mtp0: 1280/1280 exact, 0.00% divergent, 0 of 320 copy-groups disagreeing, 1474.0 tok/s against g3's 1474.3
REPLICATED.depth3_replicates_to_the_request: The speculative lane agrees to the individual request: 709/1280 exact in both arms, 44.61% divergent in both, 42 bistable slots in both, 28 oracle-on-minority in both, 44 distinct sites in both, and slot recurrence 95.45% in both. Throughput 1109.0 against 1108.7.
REPLICATED.what_that_adds: The replication is stronger than the original claim. It is not only that MTP0 came back exact twice; it is that the entire ladder outcome is reproducible across independent servers when arrival is deterministic - the same requests diverge, in the same slots, at the same sites, in the same numbers. Without a stagger, two identical arms differ by 3.1 points of copy-group rate and z = 2.93 on divergence, which is the measured noise floor. With a stagger the noise floor collapses.

the_cleaner_statement: Deterministic arrival gives deterministic output. That is the general form, and the two lanes then differ in what the deterministic output equals: at MTP0 it equals the single-stream sequential oracle, so the ladder reports 0/1280; at depth 3 it is equally reproducible but does not equal the oracle, so the ladder reports 709/1280 twice over. Speculation does not reintroduce run-to-run randomness - it moves the deterministic answer away from the sequential one.

GENERALISES_TO_THE_FULL_SUITE.arm: r2, the same 25 ms stagger on the unbiased 2026-08-25 small-context suite rather than the fragile one
GENERALISES_TO_THE_FULL_SUITE.significance: The barrier arms give 9 and 6 events per 1280, so about 7.5 expected; observed 0. Poisson P(0 | 7.5) = 5.5e-04. Weaker on its own than the fragile-suite result because the base rate is lower, and conclusive in combination with it.
GENERALISES_TO_THE_FULL_SUITE.why_it_matters: Exactness is not an artifact of a suite selected for divergence. Three arms now show it - g3 and r1 on the fragile suite, r2 on the unbiased one - at the same 14-15% throughput cost.
GENERALISES_TO_THE_FULL_SUITE.depth3_on_the_full_suite: 13.28% divergent under a barrier against 8.20% under stagger, with the oracle-free minority rate collapsing from 7.37% to 1.34% and bistable prompts from 16 to 10. The same partial effect as on the fragile suite: per-slot output becomes reproducible while the answer still differs from the sequential oracle.

THE_COST_IS_1_PERCENT_NOT_14.statement: A 5 ms stagger gives the same exactness as 25 ms at a fifteenth of the cost. The lever is essentially free.
THE_COST_IS_1_PERCENT_NOT_14.why: The cohort ramp is (concurrency - 1) * stagger: 315 ms at 5 ms against 1.575 s at 25 ms, both inside a roughly 7 s response at c64. The ramp is what costs throughput and the ordering is what buys determinism, so a stagger only needs to be long enough to order arrivals reliably, not long enough to be a large fraction of the response.
THE_COST_IS_1_PERCENT_NOT_14.depth3_at_5ms: Slot recurrence 92.83% against 95.45% at 25 ms and 33.8% under a barrier; oracle-free minority 5.28% against 4.02% and 27.31%. Slightly weaker than 25 ms on the speculative lane, and at 1173.5 tok/s against the barrier's 1171.4 - no throughput cost at all there.
THE_COST_IS_1_PERCENT_NOT_14.four_arms_now_show_exactness: g3 and r1 at 25 ms on the fragile suite, r2 at 25 ms on the full suite, r3 at 5 ms on the fragile suite. Every one certified output-identity-qualified by the harness.
